claim: Task abstention for code LLMs can be operationalized as a calibrated statistical decision rule grounded in multiple hypothesis testing, rather than a heuristic threshold on model confidence.
stance_target: prescriptive/actionable use of uncertainty signals for code LLMs
scope_conditions: code generation tasks; several open-source code LLMs; benchmark datasets not specified in abstract
quoted_support: Our approach features a calibrated abstention rule, grounded in the principles of multiple hypothesis testing.

claim: Abstention decisions can be grounded in generation consistency measured via repeated code EXECUTION outcomes rather than token log-probabilities, avoiding reliance on oracle test cases or external databases.
stance_target: execution/sampling-based signals as more trustworthy than expressed/token-level confidence
scope_conditions: syntactically diverse but semantically equivalent code generations
quoted_support: The rule assesses generation consistency through code execution outcomes, allowing it to handle syntactic diversity of semantically equivalent code without reliance on oracle test cases or external databases.

claim: The proposed abstention rule provides a rigorous, distribution-free theoretical guarantee on abstention decisions, analogous to conformal-prediction-style coverage guarantees.
stance_target: feasibility of formally-guaranteed abstention for code generation
scope_conditions: assumes access to code execution/testing environment
quoted_support: We prove that our approach provides a rigorous, distribution-free theoretical guarantee on its abstention decisions.

claim: The abstention method outperforms existing abstention techniques on accuracy and efficiency of hallucination identification, but the abstract reports no concrete numeric results (e.g., precision/recall of abstention, coverage-accuracy tradeoff).
stance_target: quantitative strength of the abstention result
scope_conditions: benchmark datasets and open-source code LLMs, unspecified in abstract
quoted_support: Results show that our method allows generative models to more accurately and efficiently identify and abstain from tasks that induce hallucination compared to existing techniques.

claim: The abstention mechanism is a binary decision (abstain vs. answer) rather than a graded, communicable confidence score, leaving open whether the underlying consistency signal could be exposed as a continuous, human-facing confidence indicator.
stance_target: gap: no graded confidence communication in this abstention framework
scope_conditions: inferred from abstract framing as an abstention/hallucination-avoidance mechanism, not a UI or trust study
quoted_support: In this paper, we study the task abstention problem, i.e., determining whether a given LLM should abstain from performing a specific code generation task to avoid likely hallucination.
